We need to determine if "Erin is not big" follows from facts and rules. We need to derive facts forward until we can answer. We start with given facts:

- Erin is smart.
- Fiona is big.
- Fiona is rough.
- Gary is not smart.
- Gary is not young.

Rules:

1. Big, furry things are not young. (If something is big and furry, then it is not young.)
2. All smart things are kind. (If something is smart, then it is kind.)
3. If Harry is smart then Harry is rough. (If Harry is smart, then Harry is rough.)
4. Furry things are green. (If something is furry, then it is green.)
5. All young things are not green. (If something is young, then it is not green.)
6. All rough, big things are furry. (If something is rough and big, then it is furry.)
7. Smart, rough things are big. (If something is smart and rough, then it is big.)
8. If something is smart and kind then it is rough. (If something is smart and kind, then it is rough.)
9. If Harry is young and Harry is kind then Harry is furry. (If Harry is young and kind, then furry.)

Note: We also have rule 8: smart and kind => rough. Rule 2: smart => kind. So smart => kind => rough. So any smart entity is kind and rough. But rule 7: smart and rough => big. So smart => big. So all smart things are big. So Erin is smart => Erin is big. So the statement "Erin is not big" is false, because we can derive Erin is big.

But we need to check if any rule could produce "Erin is not big." There's no rule that produces a not big. But we can derive Erin is big. So the negation "not big" does not follow.
